name: Module 4: sublibrary split and index PCR
description: Step 15. Takes the pooled, hairpin-ligated capsule suspension, divides it into four sublibraries, gives each its own index primer, thermocycles them in place, and then sends each indexed sublibrary off the chip through one shared outlet. 30 x 20 mm, ONE ETCH DEPTH of 0.3 mm everywhere, single fluidic layer, six ports, so it is hot-embossed in COC rather than printed: resin inhibits PCR and general-purpose resin softens near 73 C. THE SPLIT IS NOT DONE BY GEOMETRY. A symmetric manifold would split a dense capsule suspension very unevenly (sedimentation plus the Zweifach-Fung effect at a bifurcation, estimated CV 30-100%), so the four chambers are filled one at a time by an off-chip rotary valve in an interleaved palindromic order, which brings the expected CV to 3-8%. The chip is therefore four isolated reactors plus their fill lines, and the metering intelligence is off-chip. LAYOUT. The four chambers are stacked in a column, flow running west to east through each one. Each has its own fill port on the west edge (in_s1..in_s4, all at x = 2 and exactly 5 mm apart, the port-pitch floor) and its own 0.2 mm tap off its east face. The four fill lines are identical in length, 6 mm of 0.6 mm channel, so no sublibrary is favoured by its plumbing. The four taps land on ONE SHARED COLLECTION SPINE: a straight 0.6 mm channel running north along x = 18 through four tee nodes (node_1..node_4), with p_vent at its south end and out_sub, the capsule-passable product outlet, at its north end. THAT IS WHY THERE IS A SPINE AND NOT FOUR SEPARATE OUTLET RUNS. Four runs would need four more ports, and the cap is six; worse, in a single layer with no vias they would have to cross either each other or the fill lines. As drawn nothing crosses anything: fill lines run west of the chambers, taps run east of them, the spine runs north-south east of every tap. WHY SHARING A SPINE DOES NOT MIX THE INDICES. Each tap is a 0.2 mm constriction that opens abruptly into a 0.6 mm node. That step change in cross-section is a capillary stop: while a chamber fills, the displaced air escapes through the tap, along the spine and out of p_vent, and the advancing liquid halts at the widening. The spine therefore stays EMPTY OF LIQUID through filling, primer addition, mix addition and the entire thermal profile - which is the stage where short fragments leaking out of a capsule could cross-prime a neighbour and make chimeric, wrongly-barcoded molecules. Through PCR the four reactions are as isolated from each other as they were when they shared only a vent. The spine is wetted only during collection, after amplification has finished. CROSS-CONTAMINATION BETWEEN SUBLIBRARY INDICES IS BOUNDED, four ways. (1) In time. The spine carries one sublibrary at a time, driven from that chamber's own fill port with p_vent capped, so flow in the spine is one-way, toward out_sub. A sublibrary can therefore only ever meet residue from one COLLECTED BEFORE IT, never from one still sealed behind its own dry capillary stop. (2) In order. Collection runs south to north, sub_1 first: the first sublibrary crosses a virgin spine, and each later one crosses a shorter stretch of previously used channel, down to a single 4.4 mm segment for the last. (3) In volume. Each sublibrary is pushed out with an air chase, so what it leaves behind is the wetted film, not the bore. The longest collection path is about 2.7 uL of channel and the film is a few per cent of that, so the worst-case carry-over one pass can hand the next is of order 0.05 uL against roughly 4 uL of sublibrary leaving the chip - about 1%, and less for the later passes. protocols/build_library_out.py --report prints that number straight from this geometry, so it moves when the geometry moves. (4) In analysis. The four sublibraries differ only by index, so whatever carry-over there is appears as index hopping at that same bounded rate: the same order as a patterned flow cell contributes anyway, and measurable in the reads rather than invisible. If a tighter bound is ever needed, flush the spine to waste between passes; that costs run time, not geometry. Chamber volume assumes capsules are NOT swollen at this stage; if they are still at 140 um the packed volume per sublibrary is about 15 uL instead of 1.8 uL and four chambers will not fit in this envelope, in which case PCR moves to tubes. Geometry is ours; the chemistry is CapSeq, cited in protocols/module4_v1.json.

chambers.note: Sublibrary A. Filled west to east from in_s1; vents and is collected through ch_tap_1 on its east face. First to be collected, so it crosses a dry, never-used spine.
Sublibrary D. Nearest out_sub, so it is collected last and crosses only the final spine segment.
South end of the collection spine. The 0.2 mm tap opens into this 0.6 mm node: the abrupt widening is the capillary stop that holds liquid in sub_1 while letting air through to p_vent.
Spine tee for sub_2; the same 0.2 to 0.6 mm capillary stop.
Spine tee for sub_4 and the last node before out_sub.

channels.note: Vent while filling, collection route afterwards. 0.2 mm is the open-channel floor and still 2.9x a 70 um capsule, so capsules pass once the stop is burst.
Air leg, kept at 0.2 mm so it is the high-resistance arm of node_1. During collection p_vent is capped anyway and the product goes north up the spine.

ports.note: Rotary-valve position 1. All four fill ports are 5 mm apart, the port-pitch floor, and all four fill lines are the same length.

Air only, at the south end of the collection spine. Open while a chamber fills so the displaced air escapes; capped for thermocycling and capped for every collection pass, which is what makes the spine one-way toward out_sub. No liquid reaches it: each chamber's capillary stop holds during filling, and during collection the pressure gradient runs the other way.

THE PRODUCT OUTLET, and the module4 end of the module4-to-module5 hand-off. North end of the collection spine; each indexed sublibrary leaves here, one at a time, into the tubing that feeds module5_v1's in_lib. 0.8 mm drilled hole, the port floor, and 11x a 70 um capsule.
